reviews.label: A
strengths: Correct Shopify, Meta, Klaviyo and DAY18 contribution/stockout arithmetic.
Includes owners, hours, budget allocations, hypotheses, primary metrics, guardrails, stop rules and go/no-go decisions.
Brand-safe PDP copy constraints and useful questions about 15-inch fit, Klaviyo baselines and split feasibility.
issues: Caps Meta-driven DAY18 demand at 12 units/day even though the no-buffer sustainable ceiling is 6/day.
Runs four concurrent tests, including two overlapping PDP/cart-clarity changes, increasing confounding risk.
Some stop rules are relative-performance rules without a hard pre-launch inventory gate.
PDP module uses two primary metrics, increasing multiplicity risk.
critical_errors: Inventory cap and gating are misaligned with the calculated 70-unit shortfall and 6/day sustainable demand ceiling.

criterion_results.criterion: Allocations total no more than $3000; hours within 16 designer/8 developer over two weeks.
Prioritize constrained inventory and mobile product clarity; avoid running too many confounded changes.
criterion_results.reason: Calculates the inventory gap but still caps Meta at 12/day and runs four concurrent tests.

criterion_results.criterion: Distinguish operational stop rules from statistical significance; actual usable calendar.
criterion_results.reason: Includes operational stop rules, avoids significance claims and gives a 14-day calendar.

reviews.label: B
strengths: Correct core funnel, contribution-margin and rough MDE arithmetic.
Budget and hours total correctly to $3,000 and 16/8/8.
Strong uncertainty language: explicitly disclaims significance and gives useful questions.
issues: Omits the DAY18 stockout calculation: 26.25 days cover versus 35-day replenishment, with a 70-unit shortfall.
Allocates $2,200 to a Meta test while DAY18 is inventory constrained and does not set a hard stock gate.
Launches PDP, email ATC and Meta tests simultaneously, increasing confounding risk.
Hypothesis states 15-inch laptops are not fitted, which is not verified in the brand facts, though later caveated.
critical_errors: No inventory gate despite the 70-unit shortfall; $2,200 demand-generation test may accelerate stockout.
Unsupported 15-inch non-fit statement appears in proposed messaging.

criterion_results.criterion: Allocations total no more than $3000; hours within 16 designer/8 developer over two weeks.
Prioritize constrained inventory and mobile product clarity; avoid running too many confounded changes.
criterion_results.reason: No inventory cover/shortfall math; $2,200 demand test plus simultaneous PDP/email/Meta launches.

criterion_results.criterion: Distinguish operational stop rules from statistical significance; actual usable calendar.

reviews.label: C
strengths: Excellent inventory gate: 26.25-day cover, 70-unit shortfall, 6/day ceiling, and paid launch defaults to no-go.
Brand-specific mobile PDP clarity package with accurate fit, water-resistance and delivery wording.
Distinguishes operational stop/revert rules from significance and provides a usable 14-day calendar.
Keeps budget and hours within limits while sequencing tests and deferring the ATC flow expansion.
issues: Owner-hour/readout accounting has minor ambiguity around the final readout hour.
If both mobile PDP and checkout-reminder tests run, they could still interact; sequencing mitigates but does not eliminate this.
Uses all owner hours, leaving little operational slack.

Prioritize constrained inventory and mobile product clarity; avoid running too many confounded changes.
criterion_results.reason: P0 inventory gate; mobile PDP clarity first; tests are conditional and paid launch is default no-go.

reviews.label: D
strengths: Rigorous inventory and contribution gating; blocks live demand generation under the current forecast.
Explicit sample-size, power and no-significance discipline.
Brand-safe prototype copy, clear owners, cost ceilings and a usable 14-day calendar.
Correctly frames contribution margin as an upper acquisition boundary, not an approved CAC target.
issues: Very preparatory: default day-14 outcome may not include a live storefront conversion test.
Conditional P2 depends on inventory clearance that currently fails, so it may not run.
Six-participant research cannot support statistical claims, though the answer acknowledges this.

Prioritize constrained inventory and mobile product clarity; avoid running too many confounded changes.
criterion_results.reason: P0 gate blocks live demand tests; mobile research/prototype first; avoids concurrent live changes.

criterion_results.criterion: Distinguish operational stop rules from statistical significance; actual usable calendar.
criterion_results.reason: Explicit sample-size/no-significance treatment plus operational gate/stop rules and calendar.

output.summary: C and D are strongest: both prioritize the DAY18 inventory constraint, keep budget/hours within limits, and distinguish operational stops from significance. C ranks first for directly executable brand-specific mobile PDP clarity plus conditional tests; D is a very close second for rigorous inventory gating and sample-size discipline, though more preparatory. A is solid and numerically correct but risks stockout by capping demand above the sustainable 6/day and running several concurrent tests. B has correct arithmetic but omits the core inventory shortfall and over-allocates to demand generation while inventory is constrained.
